ledger.claim: This is the case POL-RD-01 warns about, and it turns on which distance field is cited. The trip_record's 20.0 km is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and may NOT be cited for the threshold test; the governing field is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, which the driver's own device recorded at 22.4 km. Measured against the booked optimal of 17.6 km, the excess is 4.8 km, or 27.27% of optimal. Both limbs of POL-RD-01 therefore pass — the excess is greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km and greater than 0.8 km absolute — and the route deviation is ESTABLISHED.

The trace is clean, so the deviation stands on it alone. EV-GPS-00112 carries 203 fixes over 100% of the trip at a 10-second sampling interval, with no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds between consecutive fixes. None of the POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) is met — no gap over 90 seconds, no jump over 500 m, no sustained interval above 30 seconds — so the trace is not impaired for policy purposes and no independent corroborating source under POL-RD-07(ii) is required.

The rider carries and discharges the initial burden under POL-RD-08. The trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown all identify trip TRP-00112 and the same 2026-08-04 evening, and the excess is measured from an unimpaired trace. The rider-side corroboration gate in POL-RD-08 does not fire either: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, far below the 4-claim trigger, so no corroboration beyond the trace is demanded. Under POL-GEN-01 no other field on the rider profile may be used to discount this claim.

Nothing in the pool exonerates any part of this excess as an external event. The only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00112-01, is MISSING — it carries no payload and weight 0.0 — so there is no named road, no validity window and no shortest_lawful_alternative_km for POL-RD-03 to run on, and limb (c) of that clause (an actual route leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor) cannot be satisfied. A general assertion that conditions were poor, unsupported by an advisory ID, does not discharge the driver's shifted burden under POL-RD-08.

The driver's rider-requested-detour defence under POL-RD-04 is not made out on this record. The chat log proves the request and the reply — the rider asked to pass by Paya Lebar Quarter and the driver answered 'ok can' — and nothing more; it is not evidence that the stop was ever made. POL-RD-04 exonerates only where the gps_trace corroborates performance by placing the vehicle within 200 m of the chat_message.waypoint_hint coordinate, and no computed fact in the derived trace package answers that test; the waypoint coordinate is fixed by the waypoint_hint field and may not be re-derived from general knowledge. The driver's counterparty statement that he 'did make the PLQ stop' is an assertion citing no artifact, and POL-RD-08 gives an assertion that cites no evidence ID no weight.

The driver's remaining explanation — that 'the app was acting up... it kept showing the trip as not started' — is not an exculpatory clause at all. POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 and POL-RD-12 are the only exonerations the route-deviation policy provides, and a malfunctioning driver app is none of them; it does not shorten the distance actually driven, which the driver's own device recorded at 100% coverage. Under POL-RD-08 that assertion points to no artifact and no clause and is discarded.

I do not put the rider's money claim higher than the arithmetic allows. On the derived money block, the POL-RD-02 recomputation on the booked optimal route — (3.80 base + 0.75 x 17.6 km + 0.28 x 28.0 min) x surge 1.0, plus the 0.80 platform fee — comes to 25.64 against a charged_total of 25.26, so the refund floors at zero and sits below the 0.50 de minimis figure. No distance refund is payable on these figures. The rider's case is that the 4.8 km of excess was real and remains unexplained, which the record supports; I ask the tribunal to record that finding rather than to read the de minimis result as an endorsement of the route driven.

Even taking the rider's case at its highest - the deviation established on the governing trace and nothing excusing it - POL-RD-02 returns her nothing. The recomputed optimal-route fare is SGD 25.64: (3.80 base fare + 0.75 x 17.6 optimal km + 0.28 x 28.0 optimal min), all at the surge multiplier of 1.0 recorded on the fare breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee and no ERP, surcharge or promo. That exceeds the SGD 25.26 actually charged, so the refund is floored at zero, below the SGD 0.50 de minimis, and the outcome on the rider's claim is NO_ACTION with the present charge left standing as POL-GEN-03 provides.

The excess is the rider's own doing and must be stripped out before the threshold test. Her in-app message at 18:33:02 asked to 'pass by paya lebar quarter first'; the platform resolved that message to waypoint VEN-PAYA-LEBAR-QUARTER at 1.3175, 103.893; and the driver answered 'ok can' at 18:33:30. That is a rider instruction, given seconds after the trip began, naming a place specifically enough to act on. Under POL-RD-04 the excess attributable to it is excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 run. The trace corroborates a stop away from the direct corridor - it shows 4.8 km of excess over the optimal route and a stationary fix, 0.0 km/h appearing in the recorded speed set, matching the driver's account of waiting about four minutes at PLQ - while the rider's bare assertion that the stop never happened is backed by no artifact at all.

Separately, the driver is owed for distance he drove but was never paid for. The fare breakdown bills the rider for 20.0 km while the governing trace records 22.4 km - a 2.4 km shortfall, above the 1.0 km trigger - so POL-RD-04 compensates the driver at SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre: 0.75 x 2.4 = SGD 1.80, already on the 0.05 grid and far below the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap. This limb is independent of the exoneration and stands whether or not the detour is excused.

The excess is 4.8 km and 27.27% of the optimal distance - above the establishment gate but below the 50% and 8.0 km materiality gate in POL-RD-01. This is therefore not a MATERIAL deviation, POL-RD-06 is not engaged on this trip, and no full-refund uplift and no driver-conduct referral is available to the rider on these facts.

There is no pass-through correction to add on the rider's side: the fare carries no ERP or toll line and no airport surcharge, the itemised gantry list is empty and every statutory total is SGD 0.00, so POL-RD-09 yields no refund and leaves the charged fare untouched.

ruling.explanation:
Addressed to both of you.

Route and threshold. The trip is TRP-00112, Tampines to One Raffles Place, on 4 Aug 2026; trip record, GPS trace and fare breakdown all carry that trip ID. The booked optimal distance is 17.6 km. The trip record's 20.0 km is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and may not be cited for the threshold test, so I use the governing trace figure of 22.4 km. The excess is 4.8 km, or 27.27% of optimal — past both POL-RD-01 gates (0.8 km absolute and 20%), so the deviation is established. It is not MATERIAL (below 50% and below 8.0 km), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged and no full-refund uplift and no driver-conduct referral arise.

The distance refund. POL-RD-02 recomputes the optimal-route fare: (3.80 base + 0.75 × 17.6 km + 0.28 × 28.0 min) = 24.84, times the surge multiplier of 1.0 read off the fare breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee, and no ERP, toll, surcharge or promo = 25.64. That is MORE than the 25.26 actually charged — the trip took 20.2 minutes against an optimal 28.0, so the time charge came in under the optimal figure — so the refund is charged_total − recomputed_fare = 0, and in any event below the 0.50 de minimis. No distance refund is payable, and POL-RD-09 adds nothing because the fare carries no ERP, toll or airport-surcharge line and the gantry list is empty.

The Paya Lebar Quarter stop. The chat log shows the request at 18:33:02 and the driver's 'ok can' at 18:33:30. POL-RD-04 would set that part of the detour aside, but only where the trace places the vehicle within 200 m of the waypoint coordinate the platform resolved for that message (1.3175, 103.893). No fact in the derived trace package answers that test and the raw coordinates are not before me, so the corroboration test cannot be run on this record and the driver's exoneration is not made out; the rider's statement that the stop was never made cites no artifact and likewise carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Nothing in the money turns on this, because the refund computes to zero on either reading.

The driver's compensation. Separately, the fare billed the rider for 20.0 km while the trace records 22.4 km. The driver drove 2.4 km for which he was not paid — above the 1.0 km trigger — so POL-RD-04 compensates him at 0.75 per unbilled kilometre: 2.4 × 0.75 = 1.80, already on the 0.05 grid and far below the 15.00 per-trip cap.

Other points. The driver's account that the app was misbehaving explains the under-billing but is not one of the route-deviation exonerations (POL-RD-03, 04, 05, 11 or 12) and does not shorten the distance actually driven. The only traffic advisory in the pool, EV-ADVIS-00112-01, is empty, so no closure defence runs. No referral fires: the deviation is not material, so POL-RD-06(c) is not engaged, and no charge line lacks a counterpart, so POL-RD-09(4) is not engaged.

Outcome. Because the moving amount is owed to the driver, the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION of SGD 1.80, and the rider's fare of SGD 25.26 stands unchanged.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
